inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E GAAP revenue for the combined Global Payments + Worldpay company (continuing operations, Issuer Solutions in discontinued ops): 9M-2026 actual $9,596.8M (10-Q Q3-2026 line 1648) plus a Q4 estimate of ~$3,350M in line with Q3's $3,306M and the Q3-2025 pro forma $3,325M. FY2026 carries only ~82 days of Worldpay in Q1 (closed 9 Jan 2026), worth roughly $120M of revenue, so the FY0 base is ~1% below a full-year run-rate; year-1 growth absorbs that. GAAP revenue runs ~4% above the company's 'adjusted net revenue' (Q3-2026: $3,306M GAAP vs $3,180M adjusted net revenue per the Analysis JSON); all margins here are on the GAAP base.
inputs.share_count_basis: 264.636M shares outstanding at 30 Oct 2026 (10-Q cover, line 1555) plus 0.52M dilutive options/awards from the Q3-2026 diluted-EPS table (line 2758) = 265.2M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC (incl. equity-award taxes) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. The 1.000% 2029 ($138.71) and 1.500% 2031 ($156.96) convertible notes are net-share settled (principal in cash) and far out of the money at the current price, so they add no shares; above ~$139 the 2029 notes would add up to (P-138.71)/P x 10.8M shares. 42.78M shares were issued to GTCR at closing (already in the count). Buybacks of $1,240M in 9M-2026 took the count from 273.4M post-close to 264.6M, so the flat count is being funded.
inputs.net_debt_note: Total long-term debt incl. current portion and $50.2M finance leases $22,536.2M at 30 Sep 2026 (Note 6, line 2290). Cash used is the $1,289.4M management identifies as available for general purposes (line 3305), NOT the $5,570.3M balance-sheet cash: the other ~$4.3B is settlement-related cash, merchant reserves and funds held for customers, matched by settlement processing obligations ($5,971M) that exceed settlement assets ($2,809M). Cross-check on the gross basis: debt 22,536 + settlement lines 1,168 - cash 5,570 - settlement assets 2,809 + settlement obligations 5,971 = $21,296M, within $50M of the figure used. Settlement lines of credit ($1,168M) are excluded from debt because they fund the settlement float, not the enterprise. Net debt / FY2026E underlying EBITDA (pre-SBC, pre-integration costs) of ~$5.66B is ~3.75x, consistent with management's stated deleveraging plan and under the 4.50x covenant ceiling.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: reported_fcf is the 9M-2026 ACTUAL (OCF $212.9M less capex $728.9M, lines 1797/1800) and is not a usable base: operating cash flow absorbed Worldpay/Issuer transaction and separation costs, liabilities assumed in the acquisition, and discontinued-operations flows (MD&A line 3313). last_fcf is instead the normalised FY2026E unlevered owner FCF built from components: revenue 12,950 x 43.7% underlying EBITDA = 5,659; less ~$1,130M acquisition/transformation/transaction cash costs (9M actual $858.8M, line 3080, plus ~$270M Q4) = 4,529; less SBC incl. equity taxes 221 = 4,308; less PP&E depreciation 3.9% = 505 -> EBIT 3,803; cash tax 17% = 647 -> NOPAT 3,156; plus D&A 505; less capex 1,000 (FY2026 guidance, line 3324) = 2,660. On that normalised basis reported_fcf_normalized_fy2026e = 2,881 and the identity last_fcf = 2,881 - 221 - 0 holds. Cross-check against guidance: the same build gives adjusted operating income of ~$5.15B (5,659 - 505), i.e. ~41.9% of ~$12.3B adjusted net revenue, against the company's Q3-2026 normalised adjusted operating margin of 42.5% and FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $13.60-13.80; the ~1pp gap is add-backs (contract-cost amortisation and similar) this model deliberately does not credit.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-Q Q3-2026 Note 11 (line 2645): share-based compensation expense from continuing operations $130.4M for 9M-2026 (annualised ~$174M), plus 'Common stock repurchased - share-based compensation plans' $35.1M for 9M-2026 (cash-flow financing line 1815; shares withheld for employee taxes on vesting), annualised ~$47M. GPN publishes no combined SBC-plus-equity-taxes figure, so the two lines are summed: ~$221M = 1.7% of FY2026E revenue. The cash-flow add-back of $91.5M (line 1782) is lower because it nets a $7.1M reversal in discontinued operations.
inputs.interest_income_note: Flows are built from EBITDA, so 'interest and other income' ($112.3M 9M-2026, line 1656; of which $77.9M is 13% PIK interest accrued on seller notes receivable, line 2807-2812) is already excluded from the flows and nothing further is stripped. The matching assets (notes receivable, equity-method investments) are added in the equity bridge instead; interest on operating cash is immaterial relative to a $21B net debt position.
inputs.buyback_note: 9M-2026 repurchases of common stock $1,240.0M (line 1813); FY2025 $1,191.0M; FY2024 $1,552.0M. Actual financing outflows, not authorisations; management targets >$2B of total capital return in 2026 (Analysis JSON guidance). Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (they fund the flat count); dividends of $1.00/share (~$265M/yr) are a distribution of the modelled FCF, not a deduction from it.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:03Z regular close (Friday); valuation dated Sunday 2026-11-08, no after-hours print involved
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. CAPM build: 10-year UST ~4.2%, beta ~1.1, ERP 5% -> cost of equity ~9.7-10%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% (weighted coupon of the senior notes and SOFR+105bp term loan; CP at 4.4%) -> ~4.1% after tax; market weights E $25.8B / D $21.2B = 55/45 -> ~7.4%. Rounded UP to 8.5% for all three scenarios because net leverage is ~3.75x into a multi-year integration, and because the CAPM weight on cheap debt flatters a company that has said it intends to de-lever. The same WACC is used in every scenario so that risk is charged once (in the probability weights), not twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): operating lease cost stays inside EBITDA as an operating expense (US GAAP), so lease liabilities (operating leases $363.9M at FY2025, 10-K line 4372) are excluded from net debt. Finance lease liabilities ($50.2M) are part of long-term debt and are therefore inside total_debt. Lease cost is not deducted again in the flows; lease_cost_pct_path is omitted.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of EBITDA), so the minority interests' share is deducted once in the equity bridge: redeemable NCI $202.2M + nonredeemable NCI $635.0M = $837.2M book (balance sheet lines 1754/1762); attributable NCI income $46.1M 9M-2026 / $55.9M FY2025. Deducted at ~15x a ~$60M run-rate = $900M rather than book, so that the deduction is on the same earnings-multiple footing as the valuation.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 1, operating company). Global Payments is a merchant-acquiring and commerce-enablement processor (Enterprise / Platforms / SMB segments from Q2-2026), not a bank, REIT or holdco, and there is no memory entry so this is the first valuation. STATUS: mid-transformation. On 9 Jan 2026 GPN acquired 100% of Worldpay (consideration $6.0B cash + 42.78M shares to GTCR, plus the Issuer Solutions business to FIS; total purchase consideration $17.0B, Note 2 line 1969) and divested Issuer Solutions to FIS for $7.5B cash + FIS's Worldpay stake. The Q1-2026 net loss of -$1,799.9M is almost entirely a $1.5B tax charge in discontinued operations on the non-deductible goodwill derecognised in the Issuer sale (Note 3 line 2109-2111) plus the first quarter of ~$750M/qtr acquired-intangible amortisation; neither is an operating signal, and neither is extrapolated. NORMALISATION: the forward margin path starts from the FY2026 underlying EBITDA margin (op income + D&A + acquisition/transformation/transaction expenses + SBC, 9M-2026 = 4,189.7 / 9,596.8 = 43.7%; Q3 alone 43.7%), and then charges the remaining integration cash costs explicitly inside the margin path (~$700M in 2027, ~$450M in 2028, ~$150M in 2029, consistent with management's 'incremental expenses through 2028', line 3120) rather than treating them as non-cash. Acquired-intangible amortisation (~$3.0B/yr, 9M $2,259M) is excluded from da_pct because it is not replaced by capex; its partial tax shield ($4.1B of Worldpay goodwill deductible, line 2031) is reflected in a 17% starting cash tax rate ramping to 21%. Capitalised contract-cost amortisation is left inside EBITDA as an operating cost. GROWTH BASE: pro forma combined revenue (as if the Transaction closed 1 Jan 2025) was $9,704M for 9M-2026 vs $9,653M for 9M-2025 (+0.5%; Q3 -0.6%), lines 2074-2081. Per the Analysis JSON, part of that is an exogenous shock: the 2026 Middle East conflict cut travel-corridor volumes (~100bp of group growth, ~400bp of Enterprise) and forced the Q2 adjusted-EPS guidance cut; management's FY2026 guidance for normalised constant-currency adjusted net revenue growth is 4-5%, with the gap to GAAP-flat made up of FX, the Payroll Solutions divestiture (Sep-2025) and the run-off of noncore portfolios. The base case starts at 4.0%, between the GAAP pro forma and the normalised guidance, and never assumes the mid-single-digit organic growth the pre-deal company used to report. HISTORY CAVEAT: FY2023-FY2025 revenue in the CSV is continuing operations (ex-Issuer), FY2022 and earlier include Issuer Solutions, and the cash-flow lines include discontinued operations throughout, so the multi-year CAGRs are indicative only. VISA PREFERRED: the Series B/C Visa preferred shares inherited from Worldpay and GPN's own are carried at zero (lines 2851-2857) and are not valued here; 90% of any Worldpay-sourced proceeds are owed to former Worldpay owners via the CVR in any case.

equity_bridge.item: Notes receivable (seller financing from the Netspend consumer and gaming disposals, 13% PIK; income excluded from EBITDA)
equity_bridge.note: Balance sheet 30 Sep 2026, line 1735; carried net of a $15.2M credit-loss allowance. Added at carrying value because the PIK interest is not in the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Equity-method investments (45% of China UnionPay Data Co. and others; equity income excluded from EBITDA)
equity_bridge.note: 10-K FY2025 line 3775, carrying value at 31 Dec 2025 (latest disclosed). Equity income ex-gain ~$70M/yr (FY2025 $120.1M incl. a $48.6M one-off), so ~15x underlying earnings is close to book.
Deducted at ~15x attributable NCI income (~$60M/yr run-rate; $46.1M 9M-2026) rather than at book, since the flows are 100% consolidated.

equity_bridge.item: Cash tax still payable on the Issuer Solutions disposal gain
equity_bridge.note: Income taxes payable rose from $117.5M (31 Dec 2025) to $1,238.5M (30 Sep 2026), line 1745, after the $1.5B tax charge in discontinued operations on non-deductible goodwill. The ~$1.12B excess over a normal payable is a real cash outflow due in Q4-2026/2027 that is in neither the flows nor net debt.

equity_bridge.item: Contingent value rights owed to former Worldpay owners (90% of Visa-disposal proceeds already realised, due 2027)
equity_bridge.note: Other noncurrent liabilities, line 2861-2862; accretes to the 2027 payment. The matching Visa preferred shares are carried at zero.

historical_growth.fcf_basis: owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (no interest-income strip; GPN has never held net cash). FY2020 1,877.9 - 148.8 = 1,729.1; FY2022 1,628.4 - 163.3 = 1,465.1; FY2025 2,038.8 - 153.6 = 1,885.2 (equity-award taxes not in the CSV history, so the historical series is SBC-only; the forward SBC charge includes them).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Midpoint between pro forma combined GAAP revenue growth (+0.5% for 9M-2026 vs 9M-2025, 10-Q Note 2, depressed by the Middle East travel shock, FX, the Sep-2025 Payroll Solutions divestiture and noncore run-off) and management's FY2026 guidance of 4-5% normalised constant-currency adjusted net revenue growth (Analysis JSON). The equity CAGR is negative because of $7.6B of buybacks since 2020 and is not usable as a growth proxy for this company.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR -3.0% vs revenue 0.7% and EPS 24.3%: divergence >30%. Equity shrank through buybacks and the FY2022 Netspend impairment; EPS was inflated by the FY2022 trough ($0.41, impairment year) and by the buyback-driven share count falling from 300.5M to 242.0M. None of the three is a clean growth read, and the revenue series changes basis at FY2023 (continuing ops only). Growth is anchored to the pro forma combined-company figures and current guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (1.7% 5yr, 8.8% 3yr) are close to reported-FCF CAGRs (1.7%, 7.8%) because SBC is only ~2% of revenue at GPN; SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. The 3yr figures are flattered by the FY2022 base, which was depressed by $615.7M of capex and the Netspend separation. All history is the pre-Worldpay entity and is not the forward base.

base.growth_note: 4.0% for 2027-28 = ~3% underlying plus ~1pp of recovery (the Q1-2026 Worldpay stub, lapping the travel-corridor shock); then fades to 2.5%. Below management's 4-5% normalised figure because that figure excludes FX and the continuing run-off of noncore portfolios, which GAAP revenue does not.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Underlying (pre-SBC) EBITDA margin 43.7% in FY2026 rising to 45.0 / 46.3 / 47.2 / 47.5% as roughly half of the gross $1.3B programme ($650M transformation run-rate by H1-2027 + $650M Worldpay synergies by end-2028, line 3121; the latter raised at Q3-2026) reaches the bottom line net of reinvestment and of what is already in the 2026 base; consistent with the ~150bp/yr of normalised adjusted operating margin expansion management guides to. LESS integration cash costs charged inside the path: ~$700M (5.2pp) in 2027, ~$450M (3.2pp) in 2028, ~$150M (1.0pp) in 2029, nil thereafter.
base.da_pct_note: Depreciation of property and equipment only (9M-2026 $373.7M = 3.9% of revenue, line 1779), converging toward the capex rate as the enlarged PP&E/software base depreciates. Acquired-intangible amortisation (~23% of revenue) is deliberately excluded: it is not replaced by capex, and its partial tax shield is in the cash tax path.
base.capex_note: FY2026 guidance ~$1.0B (line 3324) on $12.95B = 7.7%; pre-deal GPN ran 8.0% (FY2025 $617.8M / $7,706M). Eases to 7.0% as platform consolidation completes.
base.cash_tax_note: Cash tax on EBIT. GPN's pre-deal non-GAAP effective rate ran ~19%; the Worldpay purchase adds ~$4.1B of tax-deductible goodwill (line 2031) plus stepped-up intangibles, lowering the cash rate for ~15 years. 17% start ramping to the 21% US statutory rate as the shields fade. The 9M-2026 GAAP benefit (-$83.5M) reflects deal costs and the amortisation and is not the forward rate.
base.wc_note: Operating working capital (receivables, prepaids, payables) consumes ~3% of each year's revenue increase; settlement assets/obligations and funds held for customers are float, classified by GPN in financing activities, and are excluded from both the flows and (via available cash) the bridge.
base.terminal_note: 15x FCF cap (method range 12-15x for a structurally slower business) binds against Gordon (1.025/0.06 = 17.1x at 8.5%/2.5%). A 15x exit on owner FCF is roughly a 9x EV/EBITDA exit, in line with where GPN has traded for the last three years.
base.narrative: Integration delivers about half of the gross programme to margins; pro forma growth recovers from flat to 4% as the travel shock and divestitures lap, then fades to 2.5%; integration costs charged through 2029.

bull.narrative: Full $1.3B programme captured (underlying margin 50%), integration costs on the same schedule as base, travel corridors recover and Worldpay enterprise/e-commerce is cross-sold into GPN's software-led SMB base, lifting pro forma growth to 6% before fading to 3%.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: Underlying margin slips from 43.7% to 42.0% as Worldpay enterprise repricing and SMB attrition outrun cost takeout and synergies are reinvested; integration costs run ~$700M / $450M / $200M over 2027-2029 inside the path.
bear.narrative: Pro forma revenue flat in 2027 then declines 1%/yr for three years as travel/cross-border volumes stay impaired, large Worldpay enterprise merchants churn or reprice, SMB share goes to Toast/Clover/Square and e-commerce to Stripe/Adyen; stabilises flat; margin 42%; 13x terminal cap for a no-growth processor.

scenario_narratives.base: Global Payments is now a pure-play merchant acquirer (Enterprise, Platforms, SMB) of roughly $13B GAAP revenue, carrying ~$21B of net debt from the Worldpay purchase. The axes that matter are (1) whether the combined $1.3B of transformation benefit and Worldpay synergies reaches the bottom line, (2) whether pro forma revenue, flat in 9M-2026 after the Middle East travel shock, the Payroll divestiture and noncore run-off, recovers toward the 4-5% normalised rate management guides to, and (3) whether $3-4B/yr of unlevered FCF de-levers the balance sheet before anything else goes wrong. Base assumes about half the gross programme nets to margin (underlying EBITDA 43.7% to 47.5% by 2030, ~150bp/yr as guided), integration cash costs of ~$1.3B over 2027-29 are charged inside the margin path, growth runs 4% fading to 2.5%, and leverage falls below 3x by 2028 with buybacks (~$1.2-1.7B/yr) keeping the count flat.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Worldpay enterprise and e-commerce franchise plus GPN's vertical software (Genius) and Platforms (PayFac/ISV) distribution are genuinely complementary: travel corridors normalise, cross-sell lifts pro forma growth to 6% for two years, the full $650M + $650M programme is captured (underlying margin 50%), capex eases to 6.5% as platforms consolidate, and the market re-rates the company from ~7x forward adjusted EPS toward peers. Terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The deal was defensive. Worldpay's large-merchant book is low-take-rate and mobile; repricing and churn after the ownership change, continued SMB attrition to software-led competitors, e-commerce share loss to Stripe and Adyen, and a travel/cross-border portfolio that has already shown it can knock 100bp off group growth in a single geopolitical event produce three years of 1% pro forma revenue decline. Synergies are real but reinvested or competed away, so the underlying margin slips to 42% while integration costs run over. With $21B of debt the equity is a levered claim: the model still returns a positive value (no scenario hits the zero TV floor) but the bear entry price is far below the current price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 moved to 30/50/20. Bear doubled: pro forma combined revenue is flat (9M-2026 +0.5%, Q3 -0.6%), a single geopolitical event already forced a guidance cut, net leverage is ~3.75x into a multi-year integration of a $17B purchase, the market prices the stock at ~7x forward adjusted EPS, and the thesis rests on a cost programme that has not yet shown up in the GAAP numbers. Bull trimmed: it needs synergy capture, revenue re-acceleration AND a re-rating to happen together, and the Worldpay enterprise book has historically been the slower-growing, lower-margin part of the combination.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the combined company's unlevered owner FCF from its FY2026 underlying margin, charge the remaining integration cash costs explicitly, exclude acquired-intangible amortisation from the cash build but keep its tax shield, count only cash that is actually the company's (not settlement float), and bring every excluded income stream's asset and every off-flow liability (disposal tax, CVR, NCI) through the equity bridge. Growth is anchored between pro forma combined-company revenue (flat) and management's normalised guidance (4-5%), not to the pre-deal entity's history. Because the equity is a levered claim on a business in transition, the bear weight is doubled rather than the WACC inflated, so that risk is charged once.
key_risks_to_valuation: Integration execution: $650M transformation + $650M Worldpay synergies are management targets; the base case already assumes only ~half nets to margin, but the bear case shows what a reinvested or competed-away programme is worth.
Leverage: ~$21B net debt (3.75x underlying EBITDA, 4.50x covenant) with $1.4B maturing in 2027 and $2.7B in 2028; a revenue shortfall compresses equity value roughly 2x faster than EV.
Pro forma revenue flat: if the 9M-2026 +0.5% is the new run-rate rather than a shock/divestiture/run-off trough, the bear growth path is the base.

Travel and cross-border concentration: the 2026 Middle East conflict took ~100bp off group growth and ~400bp off Enterprise in one quarter and forced a guidance cut; the corridor exposure has not gone away.
Take-rate and competitive pressure in SMB (Toast, Fiserv Clover, Square) and e-commerce (Stripe, Adyen); Worldpay's enterprise merchants are mobile and price-sensitive.
Cash tax: the 17% start assumes the Worldpay step-up shields hold; a higher cash rate (21% from year 1) is worth roughly -$8/share in the base case.
One-off cash still to leave: ~$1.12B disposal tax and $362M CVR are deducted in the bridge; any further measurement-period or working-capital true-ups on the Transaction are not.

Visa preferred shares are carried at zero and not valued; segment reporting under the new structure was still being finalised at Q3-2026, so the Enterprise/Platforms/SMB mix behind the growth path may be restated.
